parsed.why: Enforced sodomy statute used as a police lever against trans women: documented arbitrary detention, prosecution, imprisonment, forced examinations amounting to torture, routine extortion, and impunity. Official hostility, no recourse. State-directed targeting, not mere paper law.

Criminalisation actively enforced (2022, Dec 2024 convictions, months in detention) with disputed 6-month–5-year penalties, no protections, general impunity. No documented police targeting of trans people specifically and no trans-specific violence data — severe but episodic.

No criminalisation, functioning civil-law institutions, sectoral protections. But zero gender-recognition route, eight refusals, and documented frontier mismatch for a trans traveller whose foreign ID says male while local records say female; social invisibility and 'gay demon' press framing.

No criminalisation; 2018 constitutional equality on sexual orientation. But record is thin: stigma noted in dated reports, no complaint mechanism, no enforcement evidence, gender identity's coverage unstated. Silence in a thin dossier is not documented safety.

Best documented positives: decriminalisation, Supreme Court gender-recognition rulings, third-gender markers, community infrastructure, pride. Offset by documented public-space discrimination and frequent physical/sexual harassment of visibly trans people, plus rising political hostility and official-linked hate speech.
